issues.legal_issue: An amendment requiring permission for executing eviction decrees does not impose a fresh-permission requirement on an execution proceeding already commenced with the required permission, unless the amendment expressly or by necessary implication applies to that pending proceeding.
material_facts: A decree-holder obtained an eviction decree concerning a tenant in a slum area and obtained permission to execute it under the law then in force.
The decree-holder filed an execution application with that permission before the amendment came into force.

While an appeal concerning the execution application was pending, the application was consigned to the record room; a later application was filed to revive it, and the court treated it as a continuation of the original pending proceeding.
The amendment came into force while the original execution proceeding was pending and changed the permission requirements for executing eviction decrees.
The tenant objected that fresh permission under the amended law was required.
issues.conclusion: The amended provision did not affect the pending execution proceeding expressly or by necessary implication. The proceeding remained governed by the law in force when it commenced, so fresh permission was not required and the tenant’s objections were rightly dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 19 of the Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1956, as it stood before its substitution by the Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Amendment Act, 1964, a decree-holder required prior written permission to execute an eviction decree. The substituted section 19 also required permission for executing decrees obtained in proceedings instituted before the amendment. However, absent express words or necessary implication that an amendment applies to pending proceedings, the parties’ rights in a proceeding are determined under the law in force when it commenced. The court found no such intention in the substituted section: it neither provided for a stay nor otherwise clearly varied rights in pending proceedings. Applying the amended requirement could also leave a decree-holder without a remedy if a fresh execution application were time-barred. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.eviction_decree_execution: The proceeding seeks to execute a decree for eviction of a tenant from premises in a protected area.
predicates.execution_application_started_before_ame: The decree-holder commenced the execution proceeding before a change in the governing law took effect.
predicates.required_permission_obtained_before_appl: The decree-holder obtained the permission required by the law in force before filing the execution application.
predicates.later_application_continues_original_pro: A later filing seeks to revive or continue the original execution proceeding rather than commence a new proceeding.
predicates.amendment_lacks_clear_application_to_pen: The amendment does not expressly or by necessary implication apply its new requirements to proceedings already pending.

issues.definition: When an eviction-decree execution proceeding was commenced with the permission then required and a later filing continues that proceeding, a change in law that does not clearly apply to pending proceedings does not require fresh permission.
